doc.title: Chuck Israels interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 11, 2021

title: Writing for group interaction
summary: Israels says he writes for ensemble interplay and the personalities of instruments rather than for solos.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Okay. Those ideas, when you conceive of a composition, perhaps it’s at the piano or perhaps it’s taking a walk, anything in between those two, but the arrangement of it, the arrangement of the initial idea, do you think that’s where those textures and so forth come from?

Yes. They’re interesting to me. I’m particularly interested in what an ensemble of instruments does together as a group. I’m certainly affected by soloists and what they can do, but I tend to write things that are focused on group interaction. Things that soloists can do often are best left to them, I mean not entirely, there are plenty of people who write wonderful solo music and I’m not saying that I never write that, but I’m more interested in, oh I can write this for this person to do or this instrument or generally I think of them as having certain kind of personalities in an abstract way. personality does this, and this personality responds in this way, and then the group, it’s the interaction is what’s interesting to me. Most interesting.
